hypothesis: E1 XG-HGB: a supervised HistGradientBoosting detector on a label-free 47-channel multi-physics stack whose novel channel is the magnetic x gravity cross-gradient boundary (sqrt(|grad RTP||grad gravity|)*(1-|sin theta|)), plus Hessian line responses, Miller-style tilt proxies, GeoDAWN radiometric ratios and correctly band-indexed 3DEP LiDAR dipole features, will recover blind faults that single-physics ridge surfaces miss, when emitted as 37,654 spacing>=3px dots outside a B=2 catalogue gate.
mechanism: Cross-gradient penalises boundaries seen in only one potential field; multi-physics HGB fuses that with topographic/LiDAR scarps. Dotted spacing>=3px emission matches the 300 m triangular DTI kernel (beta=0.8 FN cost dominates alpha=0.2 FP cost, so breadth of coverage is favoured). B=2 prune removes dots whose expected credit is below the alpha*DTI marginal bar near the already-mapped catalogue.
named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts (magnetite-bearing basalt flows / gravity basement lithology changes), roads and mine benches in LiDAR, paleo-shoreline/terrace risers, and drainage-aligned valley chains can all produce coincident mag-gravity edges and scarps without a Quaternary fault.
